conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. You’re here because of nausea, vomiting, and feeling shaky. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve been vomiting clear stuff for two days, couldn’t keep anything down. I was up all night with back pain and nausea. This morning I felt trembly and shaky after taking my Zoloft.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You were on sertraline, tramadol, and Zofran. There’s a concern that these together might have caused a reaction called serotonin syndrome.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Serotonin syndrome? Is that serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can be, but yours seems mild. Toxicology reviewed your case and didn’t think it was full-blown. Still, we’ll stop tramadol and Zofran to be safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I need something for nausea. I’ve had gastroparesis for years.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll use Reglan instead of Zofran. It’s safer for you. And we’re giving IV fluids because you’re dehydrated from vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. My heart’s been racing too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your heart rate was in the 120s. That could be from dehydration or the serotonin concern. We’re monitoring you on telemetry.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I also have bad back pain from an old car accident. I’ve been taking Dilaudid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We know. But long-term opioids aren’t recommended for you. We’re switching to a lidocaine patch, Tylenol, and tizanidine at night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will that be enough? The pain keeps me up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We hope so. Tizanidine helps with muscle spasms and can aid sleep. But avoid driving when you take it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. What about my diabetes? I couldn’t take my insulin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve been giving insulin through your IV. Your sugars are stabilizing. No ketones in blood, but we saw some in urine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My A1C was 10.9 last time. I know it’s high.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll help you manage that. You’ll go back to your home insulin regimen when you can eat again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve also been on antibiotics for H. pylori. I missed a few doses before coming in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re continuing amoxicillin and levofloxacin. You’ll finish the course after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve had that before and it helped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a chest X-ray. It’s clear—no pneumonia or fluid. Your ultrasound was also normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the urine test? I saw bacteria.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You had some bacteria and white cells, but no symptoms of infection. It’s called asymptomatic bacteriuria—no treatment needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my mood’s been low. I was on Zoloft, but now it’s stopped?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We paused sertraline because of the possible reaction. Psychiatry thinks you may benefit from restarting it later, without tramadol or Zofran.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I do feel better with it, but the nausea made me stop before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll coordinate with your PCP and psychiatrist. It’s important you follow up after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs are improving. Heart rate is down to 95, and you’re less shaky.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel a bit better. Can I try eating something?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start with clear liquids. If that goes well, we’ll advance your diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’m so tired of being NPO.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You tolerated apple juice and broth. We’re moving you to a soft diet—mashed potatoes, applesauce.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. My back feels a little better with the new meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep monitoring. Your insulin doses are adjusting with your meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs this morning look great. Anion gap is normal, no ketones. Heart rate is 88.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t vomited since yesterday morning. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly tomorrow. We want to make sure you can keep food down and your sugars stay stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my meds when I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll continue amoxicillin and levofloxacin for four more days, omeprazole daily. Stop tramadol and Zofran for good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my Zoloft?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your PCP will decide if and when to restart it. But never with tramadol or Zofran.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You have appointments with your PCP, a pain specialist, and social work. They’ll help coordinate care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve missed some before. I’ll try this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s very important. You’ve had multiple admissions. A team approach can help prevent that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re discharging you today. You’re eating, sugars are stable, and symptoms resolved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Remember: no tramadol or Zofran. Use the lidocaine patch, tizanidine, and Tylenol for pain. Take your antibiotics as directed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I’ll call to reschedule if I can’t make a follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Your health depends on these appointments. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. A nurse will go over your discharge instructions and medications now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your urine culture was negative, so no infection. And your anemia is mild, likely from chronic disease. Monitor it with your PCP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, I’ll keep that in mind.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And your blood pressure was a bit high. Keep taking lisinopril daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I sometimes forget, but I’ll try to be more consistent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That would help. We’re all here to support you. Just keep in touch.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go home. The nurse will finalize everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Glad to hear it. Take care of yourself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If symptoms return—vomiting, shaking, high sugars—come back right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I don’t want to be back here soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We don’t either. That’s why follow-up is key.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand. I’ll do my best.
